title: The first-order part of the Ordered Variable Word theorem
summary: An ordered $ω$-variable sequence over a finite alphabet~$A$ is an infinite sequence over the extended alphabet $A \sqcup \{ x_0, x_1, \dots \}$, where each variable kind appears at least once, and the last occurrence of $x_i$ appears before the first occurrence of $x_{i+1}$. The Ordered Variable Word theorem states that for every finite coloring of the words over a finite alphabet~$A$, there is an ordered $ω$-variable sequence~$W$ over~$A$ such that every word induced by substituting variables with letters, and cutting before the first undefined variable, has the same color.
